blocking_questions: The prediction table has four rows with one predicted number each (design:37-42), but the Cells section produces 216 steered runs -- 36 steered numbers per model per benchmark (design:85-86). Which of those 36 is compared against the '77', and is that selection rule fixed in the file before the run?

Read the abandonment criterion (design:231) against rows 3 and 4. Explanation A predicts CHAIR unchanged at 20 and 17 -- identical to the baseline column. The criterion abandons the truthfulness hypothesis 'if baseline performance showed no difference on these benchmarks than when steering is applied.' Which benchmarks does 'these benchmarks' cover, and is there an outcome that both confirms A and satisfies the criterion?

Predicted deltas are 7, 4, 0, and 4 points (design:39-42); n is 450/600/500 and the Sample size section states no power argument (design:213-217). At n=450, what size of accuracy change can you separate from zero, and how do you know? Then what that becomes across 36 comparisons per model per benchmark.

Assumptions says 'I can't think of any assumptions that would need to be checked' (design:239). The design turns free-text into tp/fp/tn/fn on two models with different output conventions, and captions into object counts through a fixed synonym list (metrics.py:329-335). AMBER 450 is 276 gold-no and 174 gold-yes (pinned_amber_disc_450.json:475-476). For the yes/no parser, the object parser, and the gold-label split -- what result would tell you the design is not measuring what the table's rows say it measures?
corrections: The question states the method under test is 'the mean difference in truthful versus hallucinated captions' (design:13,15). The directions the design consumes are not mean differences: metadata.json records steer_reconstruction = 'live_pc1_plus_mean' and a sign convention reading 'no mean-diff sign-align'. Primitives declares 'none', so no mean-difference direction is produced under this spec.
design:48 says 'I expect the relevant performance increase in cells 1 and 3'. The table gives cell 3 (LLaVA CHAIR) as 20 under baseline and 20 under A -- no increase.

The stated total of 216 steered + 6 baseline runs counts POPE 600 as one run per cell. run_eval.py:33 takes a single --pope_split and eval_runner.py:284 keys output pope_{split}, so POPE is three invocations per cell.

The Cells table fixes the intervention as additive but names no hook site. interventions/__init__.py:29-33 registers vti_textual_additive_mlp and vti_textual_additive_layer; steer.py:11 defines HOOK_SITES = ('mlp','layer'); the default is hook_site='mlp' (intervention.py:39).
code_gaps_verified: Gap 1 confirmed: intervention.py:12-20 imports only directions and directions_v2; directions_partition is not imported by intervention.py or run_eval.py.
Gap 2 confirmed: intervention.py:151-160 calls vti_hook_ctx without layer_indices; run_eval.py:21-77 exposes no layer flag.
Gap 3 confirmed with a correction: _flip_counts exists only at rotation_strength.py:132-161 and returns four flip counts, not the two the spec names.
Gap 4 confirmed: run_eval.py:50 defaults --chair_max_new_tokens to 64 while --max_new_tokens defaults to 256.
No additional blocking gaps. Generation is greedy throughout (do_sample=False), so run-to-run generation variance is not a source of spread.

turns.content:
To respond to your questions, one, for blocking is not legitimate. The point of the prediction cells is to just give a general impression of how the data will look. It doesn't have to be as specific as running 36 steered runs. and if that's not the case given the current definitions of the harnesses then I want to know because these four rows that I've provided should be enough to get the idea across. I definitely do not want to have to write 36 steered numbers in the future when writing specs. 2. I don't really understand what you're asking. I don't know what you're asking when you say that, is there an outcome that both confirms A and satisfies the criterion? What criterion? As far as what benchmarks does the benchmarks cover, there's three benchmarks in this repository currently that are tested for hallucination mitigation, Pope, Amber, and Chair, and only describing performance on amber regarding discriminative stuff is sufficient because Pope was also a discriminative benchmark and they're basically testing the same abilities of the model. Same point about 3 as 1, the prediction table, I don't want it to be an extensive, extremely specific requirement that requires me to do things like consider sample size and prediction deltas and whatnot. like the relative change between the performances that each column provides should be enough to get my predictions across if again if there's a harness that prevents this sort of behavior then let me know because I'm not interested in providing that much detail in these prediction tables going forward. That's actually a good point. The fact that the amber 450 is not balanced in terms of yes-no ratio or gold-no-go, gold-yes ratio means that the yes ratio needs to be reported and the results to make sense of how the performance of the models change under steering Under the gold no and gold yes subsets, The assumption being that the model should perform as well on the gold no subset as the gold yes subset.

As far as the corrections, I'm saying that per the spec, I want the question that this experiment tests to be the hypothesis where the steering vector is the mean difference in truthful versus hallucinated captions. That's the specification that I'm giving, meaning that if this direction doesn't exist, i.e. if the mean difference, the raw mean difference between truthful and hallucinated captions is not saved, it should be recalculated and saved. I'm specifically not trying to test the steering vector construction using PCA. It was a mistake that primitives declares none in that case. The primitives used should be the saved activations, and the same 5100, 200, and 500 sets of demo examples that are already defined should be used to create these more raw steering vectors that don't use PCA at all to create the steering vector. As far as my statement, I meant that the relative performance increase between the baseline and explanation A when looking at row 1 versus row 3, not cell 1 and cell 3, my apologies, should Give evidence as to whether explanation A is true because a truthfulness vector should not change the impact significantly on a generative benchmark, but it should on a discriminative benchmark. Go ahead and change the number of counts of steered and baseline runs then so that the splits are obvious. I don't really care. Good catch. The cells table should specify that the addition should be done at MLP. It was my mistake earlier in research in doing this to specify a separate additive case at the post-residual stream, or what we're calling the layer site. These really have no difference when it comes to additive steering. adding pre-residual stream or post-residual stream will have the same exact outcome. In fact, this would be something that would be good to note as a code gap, that hook sites at layer should be maybe renamed to residual stream, and that additive textual steering, or rather linear additive textual steering, should not have a difference in site capability. It should be added always at the MLP site, let's say, to avoid confusion.

Answered the two harness questions, verified two of Alex's claims against the code before recording them, then applied eight edits to the spec.

Harness answers: (1) nothing in the harness requires 36 numbers -- design_template.md:25-26 asks only for 'direction and rough magnitude'. What let the question fire is that check 1 of examine-design.md says 'an entry for every condition', and 'condition' is ambiguous between a table row and a design arm. (2) The effect-size requirement is not from the prediction table -- it is the Sample size field itself (design_template.md:151-157) plus check 5 of the command, so loosening the table would not remove it.

Verified claims: the hook-site equivalence holds for additive and only for additive (steer.py:44-45 returns x + alpha*d_hat; the decoder layer's only consumer of the MLP output is the residual add; the rotation variants renormalise against x.norm() at steer.py:47,72). The mean-difference directions cost zero forward passes -- 5100 cached activation files per model, verified present for both.

Also noted once, without pressing: the granularity objection and the selection rule are different things, and the file still does not say which of the 72 arms is compared against the 77.

turns.content:
About the prediction table granularity, yes, I'd like you to make this change because I think it's a good idea to include something like a prediction table, but to make me have to write it with the granularity of every possible sweep configuration is too much. I think the point of it is really just to display that I understand how the possible explanations for the hypothesis that I am testing will appear in the result data.

As for the effect size, I'm frankly a bit stuck on how to decide what to do about it because Maybe it's fair to expect me to write something general about how the size of the data or the increase in the size of the data specifically the evaluation sets or the sets of data used to calculate the steering vectors is fair, but but any level of detail about prediction would be too much because it's just too much to expect that someone will make an accurate or even semi-accurate prediction about how increasing n or multiplying n by 5 or 10 or something will affect the results. That's just something that you kind of examine after you run the experiment with a general idea of how increasing or decreasing sample size will affect the outcome. Otherwise the edits are good.

turns.proposal_returned_to_alex: Two different things sit under 'sample size': (a) resolution of the instrument -- the smallest difference n can separate from noise, which follows from n alone (at n=450 with a baseline near 0.70 the binomial SE is about 2.2 points); and (b) scaling of the effect with n, which is a prediction about the result. The template only ever asked for (a); what made it read as (b) is that the design has two different n's. Proposed a replacement Sample size field keeping the one-line arithmetic and explicitly excluding the forecast.

turns.content:
Okay, I'm not sure exactly what happened, but I ran a new chat that ran the command plan on the design spec that we validated together and that we edited together, designs/07_30_26/steering_vector_visual_reasoning_validation.md. The plans that actually resulted from this design spec are under implementation_plans/7-30-26, and I'm particularly interested in the sanity check plan that proposes 10 different sanity checks in regards to our design spec. I'm curious as to what actually caused the planning agent to want to perform so many checks, and in particular, checks that seem to be mainly checks of how the code runs, which can literally just be validated by the agent itself while it's creating the plan, or are checks that are literally validations of how the code works or how artifacts are saved or what their contents are, all of which can be looked up by looking at the implementation markdown file, or by asking me beforehand such that I can provide an assumption to the agent in case it's unsure about some of the parts of the spec. For example, check2 is completely useless because I myself am sure that the four partition blocks are actually disjoint and I would wager that the implementation markdown already lists this explicitly and if it doesn't, it should be in there anyway.

for context my old agent except was to maintain and implementation markdown file whenever a change in the implementation the online you for this repository was changer something and the research should contain results experiments course and my son this repository. I'm making references to it mainly because I'm assuming that the planning agent is not reading this at all because so many of these checks look like the work of someone Who has never seen the repository before or ever worked with it would want to make Because they have no context about it.

I want to be clear all I did when I opened the new chat instance to create these plans was run the plan command on our design spec I didn't say or do anything else to the files nor did I have any additional turns with the chat session that the planning sub-agent was called in

can you try to provide some insight on why there's so many checks that are essentially useless for someone who actually has some context about the implementation of the repository?

Diagnosed five causes, with citations, and corrected one part of the framing.

1. The sanity-check instruction has no ceiling and an escalation clause. planner.md:154-164 names six categories, gives no cap, and closes with 'this project has run a full experiment on a broken data premise'. The examiner has a hard cap of three to five and an explicit 'zero is legitimate'; the planner has neither, and a cap is the only thing that forces prioritisation.

2. 'Where the checks are substantial, write them as their own plan file' made the container bigger than the content. Once that branch was taken, three checks in a separate document would look thin and ten looks proportionate.

3. IMPLEMENTATION.md is pointed at once, in the wrong section, for the wrong job. planner.md:117-123 sits under Grounding and its object is identifiers -- it is a spell-checker for names. Nothing says the file is a record of already-established repo state that can retire a check. It is absent from CLAUDE.md, WORKFLOW.md, and WORKFLOW_MAP.md entirely.

4. Nothing distinguishes 'verify it now' from 'write a check for later'. The planner holds Read, Grep, Glob, Bash. Checks 2, 8, 9 are file reads it could have done during planning.

5. The whitelist does not cover checks. planner.md:72-83 bounds cells, conditions, metrics, models, benchmarks, item sets, seeds, hyperparameters. Sanity checks are not on that list, so the one 'do not add things' mechanism does not reach the section that inflated.

Correction to the framing: these are not the work of an agent with no repo context. Seven of the ten trace to something it was handed -- checks 1 and 2 to the Primitives section rewritten in this session, 3 to the new primitive, 4 to Code gap 2, 5 to the standing device_map constraint at planner.md:127, and 6 and 7 to the Assumptions section Alex added in this session. Only 8, 9, 10 are not in the spec. The mechanism is that this session roughly tripled the surface the planner enumerates over, with no cap and no rule permitting a read to close a check instead of opening one.

turns.content:
Yeah, let's keep the number of sanity checks to, let's say, 5 at a maximum, with clear instructions that sanity checks are not something that should be added for the sake of adding for a new code base that is necessary to run to implement the design spec needs to be checked to validate an assumption that the experiment is based on. And that assumption should not be relative to the code implementation or the nature of at the existing artifacts that might be reused in separate experiments because all of this information is for sure in the implementation markdown. I think the implementation markdown should definitely be mentioned in the ClaudeMD so that any agent, no matter what, has to read it for context without the entire repo. This is what grounds any agent who inevitably is assisting me in doing something with the codebase to know what already exists on disk, which is largely a representation of where this project is in general.

Finally, if there is an instruction for Cursor, the implementation agent, to update the implementation markdown after it finishes performing an implementation for a plan definitely include a hard rule for it to add to the implementation file as it's been structured up until this point. the other things that you propose are also useful as well please add those too.

Applied four sets of edits: the five-check cap in both planner.md and plan.md written identically so they cannot drift; IMPLEMENTATION.md as required reading at the head of CLAUDE.md's Infrastructure section; and a hard rule on the Cursor side that every finished plan ends with an IMPLEMENTATION.md update following the file's existing structure. Also fixed a stale handoff path in the Cursor rule. verify_harness.sh still passes 14/14.

Noted that the ten-check plan under implementation_plans/7-30-26/ is untouched -- regenerating it means rerunning /plan, which writes a new dated plan alongside the existing ones rather than replacing them.

workflow_observations: The examiner gate held: the bypass log was checked and contained no entry dated today for this design, so the examination proceeded normally rather than being short-circuited.

The examiner held its scope. It stated that two prediction columns were identical and asked which cell separates them, without concluding what the identity implied. It stated factual discrepancies as statements and questions as questions.
Two examiner questions were rejected on their premise by Alex, and one was rejected as unclear. Rejection led to harness changes rather than to the examiner being overruled case-by-case.
One examiner correction (the PCA-vs-mean-difference discrepancy) changed the experiment's declared primitive from 'none' to a new artifact, which is the largest single consequence of the examination.

Two of Alex's own claims were verified against the code before being written into the spec: the additive hook-site equivalence (holds for additive only) and the availability of cached activations (5100 files per model, so zero forward passes).
The session declined to add an unrequested requirement to the design template, drafted it, removed it, and reported the omission rather than imposing it.
One tool call was rejected by the user mid-session and re-applied with the requested addition.
The user interrupted one turn to commit intermediate work, then resumed.

The ten-check sanity plan produced by a separate session was diagnosed by reading the harness files rather than the plan alone; seven of the ten checks traced to instructions the planner was handed, which reframed the cause from 'no repo context' to 'no cap over an enlarged surface'.
open_items_at_session_end: The design spec still does not state which of the 72 steered arms supplies the number compared against the prediction table's entries. Raised twice, left to Alex.
